    # and D carry op 30's exact semantics (F the
    # [id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency] shape, L the
    # worst-utilization-increase cap, C the per-scenario migrated-demand
    # cap, R the per-flow per-scenario cumulative reroute cap, D the
    # minimum clock gap); W and Q are non-boolean integers in
    # 0..MAX_COST, W the inclusive window width behind the event clock
    # and Q the largest number of one flow's reroutes whose clocks lie
    # in [e-W, e] within one scenario.
    #
    # Every input validates first, exactly as op 30 (shapes in the
    # command entry; the h[b] reference/endpoint/scenario checks,
    # clocks, and event t/p here), then simulation walks from h[b] in E
    # order under non-decreasing event clocks. Beside op 30's flat
    # per-(scenario, flow) cumulative counts and last-reroute clocks,
    # each scenario - the no-failure scenario and each S scenario,
    # never merged - keeps its own flat per-flow non-decreasing
    # reroute-clock sequence. A non-idempotent event routes both sides
    # per scenario and a flow reroutes at the event clock exactly on
    # op 30's predicate (reachable on both sides, different complete
    # node paths). For the candidate window the sequence first drops
    # clocks strictly below e-W, then appends e for a reroute; the flow

    # an equal-state event add no record (the equal-state row is status
    # 1 with an empty impact and changes nothing). The event passes
    # only when it satisfies every op 30 gate (reachability, bandwidth,
    # per-flow maxLatency, C, L, R, and D) and every flow's window
    # passes in every scenario. The impact is op 30's
    # [oldWorst, newWorst, delta, scenarios] with each scenario row in
    # op 30's exact order gaining maxWindowMoves after maxMoves and
    # each flow row gaining windowStart, windowMoves, windowPass after
    # intervalPass; the failing event's rendered counts, clocks, and
    # window lengths are the candidate post-event values. At the first
    # failing event simulation stops at once and the whole batch

    # Version/history append, duplicate-resend recognition, the

def _config_gapmig_gate_batch(pack_path, pack, v, history, mode, base,
                              events, flows, limit_ppm, scenario_specs,
                              moved_ppm, move_cap, min_gap):
    # Batched hotload with op 29's full compound-failure and cumulative
    # reroute gates plus a per-flow per-scenario minimum reroute
    # interval (config op 30): [30, m, b, E, F, S, L, C, R, D].
    # m, b, E, F, S, L, C, and R carry op 29's exact semantics (F the
    # [id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency] shape, L the
    # worst-utilization-increase cap, C the per-scenario migrated-demand
    # cap, both in parts per million, R the per-flow per-scenario
    # cumulative reroute cap); D is a non-boolean integer in
    # 0..MAX_COST, the smallest clock gap allowed between two reroutes
    # of one flow within one scenario.
    #
    # Every input validates first, exactly as op 29 (shapes in the
    # command entry; the h[b] reference/endpoint/scenario checks,
    # clocks, and event t/p here), then simulation walks from h[b] in E
    # order under non-decreasing event clocks. Beside op 29's flat
    # per-(scenario, flow) cumulative counts, each scenario - the
    # no-failure scenario and each S scenario, never merged - keeps its
    # own flat per-flow last-reroute clock; a slot is unset until that
    # flow's first reroute there. A non-idempotent event routes both
    # sides per scenario and a flow reroutes at the event clock exactly
    # on op 29's predicate (reachable on both sides, different complete
    # node paths). The first reroute always passes; a later reroute
    # passes only when event_clock - last_clock >= D. D=0 adds no
    # restriction, so two reroutes at the same clock fail the second
    # only when D > 0. A non-reroute and an equal-state event update
    # neither count nor clock. The event passes only when it satisfies
    # every op 29 gate (reachability, bandwidth, per-flow maxLatency,
    # C, L, and R) and every flow's interval passes in every scenario.
    # An equal-state event is idempotent (row status 1, an empty
    # impact) and changes no state. The impact is op 29's
    # [oldWorst, newWorst, delta, scenarios] with each scenario row in
    # op 29's exact order and each flow row gaining previousMoveClock,
    # gap, intervalPass after moves; the failing event's rendered
    # counts/clocks are the candidate post-event values. At the first
    # failing event simulation stops at once and the whole batch
    # rejects: event row and batch status 2, old/new both the pre-call
    # v, applied false, config the pre-call pack, and PACK untouched in
    # either mode; the count and clock arrays then die with the call.
    #
    # Version/history append, duplicate-resend recognition, the
    # preview/commit difference, and the single atomic replace follow
    # op 16/27/28/29 exactly. For B events, S scenarios, K distinct
    # flow sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links the bound is
    # O(B(S+1)(K(V^2+A) + FV + A)) time and
    # O(KV + FV + A + (S+1)F) extra space besides the returned result.
    if base > v:
        fail(5)
    base_topo = history[base][1]
    base_node_set = set(base_topo["nodes"])
    for item in flows:
        if item[1] not in base_node_set or item[2] not in base_node_set:
            fail(5)
    prepared = _config_compound_prepare(base_topo["nodes"],
                                        base_topo["links"], flows,
                                        scenario_specs)

def _config_linkdiv_gate_batch(pack_path, pack, v, history, mode, base,
                               events, flows, limit_ppm, scenario_specs,
                               moved_ppm, move_cap, min_gap,
                               window_width, window_cap, demand_cap,
                               distinct_cap, count_cap, path_cap,
                               link_cap):
    # Batched hotload with op 35's full compound-failure, cumulative,
    # minimum-interval, per-flow burst-window, per-scenario cumulative
    # migrated-demand window, per-scenario distinct-affected-flow
    # window-demand, per-scenario distinct-affected-flow COUNT, and
    # per-flow per-scenario distinct complete-PATH window gates plus a
    # per-flow per-scenario distinct directed-LINK window gate (config
    # op 36): [36, m, b, E, F, S, L, C, R, D, W, Q, H, U, N, X, Y]. The
    # first sixteen entries carry op 35's exact validation and semantics
    # (F the [id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency] shape, L the
    # worst-utilization-increase cap, C the per-scenario migrated-demand
    # cap, R the per-flow per-scenario cumulative reroute cap, D the
    # minimum clock gap, W the inclusive window width behind the event
    # clock, Q the per-flow per-scenario reroute count cap in [e-W, e],
    # H the per-scenario summed retained-demand cap, U the per-scenario
    # distinct retained-demand cap, N the per-scenario distinct
    # retained-flow count cap, and X the per-flow per-scenario distinct
    # complete-path cap); Y is a non-boolean integer in 0..MAX_COST, the
    # largest number of distinct directed links - the adjacent-node
    # directed edges contributed by every retained candidate path - a
    # single flow may still touch in the closed window [e-W, e] of one
    # scenario. The gate catches the reroute- and path-count gates' blind
    # spot: a handful of different complete paths can still strangle too
    # many forwarding links, and the distinct-link union, not either
    # record count, is what Y caps.
    #
    # Every input validates first, exactly as op 35 (shapes in the
    # command entry; the h[b] reference/endpoint/scenario checks,
    # clocks, and event t/p here), then simulation walks from h[b] in E
    # order under non-decreasing event clocks. Beside op 35's separate,
    # never merged per-(scenario, flow) cumulative counts, last-reroute
    # clocks, (clock, demand) reroute sequences, retained-demand sums,
    # (clock, complete-path) sequences, and path->retained-count
    # tables, each (scenario, flow) slot keeps its own (clock,
    # directed-links) sequence and a directed-link->retained-count
    # table. A non-idempotent event routes both sides per scenario and a
    # flow records one candidate at the event clock exactly on op 35's
    # predicate (reachable on both sides, different complete node
    # paths); that record contributes the directed links of adjacent
    # nodes on the candidate path. Processing the event first drops, for
    # every slot, link records whose clocks are strictly below e-W (a
    # record on the edge e-W stays; the demand, path, and link windows
    # trim and append in lockstep), then appends (e, that flow's new
    # directed links) for a reroute. The same directed link referenced
    # by several paths or by repeated paths inside the window counts
    # once: its table count rises for each retained record referencing
    # it and the link leaves the set only when the last record carrying
    # it slides out. Records of different flows and of different
    # scenarios are never merged. A non-reroute, an unreachable
    # migration, an unchanged path, and an equal-state event add no
    # record. windowDistinctLinkCount is the flow's post-trim distinct
    # retained directed-link count and the flow passes the
    # link-diversity gate only when it is at most Y; Y = 0 rejects every
    # flow that still retains a link record. The equal-state row is
    # status 1 with an empty impact and changes nothing. The event
    # passes only when it satisfies every op 35 gate (reachability,
    # bandwidth, per-flow maxLatency, C, L, R, D, Q, H, U, N, and X)
    # and every flow's distinct link count is at most Y in every
    # scenario. The impact is op 35's [oldWorst, newWorst, delta,
    # scenarios] with each scenario row gaining maxWindowDistinctLinks
    # inserted after maxWindowDistinctPaths and before pass, and each
    # flow row gaining windowDistinctLinkCount and linkDiversityPass
    # inserted after windowDistinctPathCount and before
    # pathDiversityPass; the failing event's rendered counts, clocks,
    # windows, window demand, distinct demand, distinct count, path
    # windows, distinct path counts, link windows, and distinct link
    # counts are the candidate post-event values. At the first failing
    # event simulation stops at once and the whole batch rejects: event
    # row and batch status 2, old/new both the pre-call v, applied
    # false, config the pre-call pack, and PACK untouched in either mode
    # with no temp file; the per-batch arrays then die with the call.
    #
    # Version/history append, duplicate-resend recognition, the
    # preview/commit difference, and the single atomic replace follow
    # op 16/27/28/29/30/31/32/33/34/35 exactly. For B events, S
    # scenarios, K distinct flow sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links
    # the bound is O(B(S+1)(K(V^2+A) + FV + A)) time and
    # O(KV + FV + A + B(S+1)FV) extra space besides the returned
    # result.
    if base > v:
        fail(5)
    base_topo = history[base][1]
    base_node_set = set(base_topo["nodes"])
    for item in flows:
        if item[1] not in base_node_set or item[2] not in base_node_set:
            fail(5)
    prepared = _config_compound_prepare(base_topo["nodes"],
                                        base_topo["links"], flows,
                                        scenario_specs)
    last_e = None
    for item in events:
        e = item[0]
        if last_e is not None and e < last_e:
            fail(5)
        last_e = e
        _validate_topology(item[1], metrics=True)
        if not _is_policy(item[2]):
            fail(5)

    flow_count = len(flows)
    total_demand = 0
    for item in flows:
        total_demand += item[3]
    cur_version = base
    cur_t = history[base][1]
    cur_p = history[base][2]
    # As in op 35 the batch is only defined from a failure-feasible
    # h[b]: every flow routable in every scenario within its
    # maxLatency and every link within its bandwidth there.
    (_, _, _, cur_reachable, cur_no_over, cur_latency_ok, _) = \
        _config_clatency_assess(cur_t["nodes"], cur_t["links"], flows,
                                flow_count, prepared, False)
    if not cur_reachable or not cur_no_over or not cur_latency_ok:
        fail(5)

    # Per-(scenario, flow) op 35 cumulative migration counts,
    # last-reroute clocks, retained (clock, demand) reroute sequences,
    # retained demand sums, retained (clock, complete-path) sequences,
    # and path->retained-count tables, plus op 36's parallel retained
    # (clock, directed-links) sequences and link->retained-count tables.
    # Scenario index 0 is the no-failure scenario then the prepared
    # scenarios in S order, each block F entries in F order. Counts
    # start at zero, clocks unset (None), sequences/tables empty, and
    # demand sums zero.
    slot_count = (len(prepared) + 1) * flow_count
    cur_moves = [0] * slot_count
    cur_clocks = [None] * slot_count
    cur_windows = [deque() for _ in range(slot_count)]
    cur_window_demand = [0] * slot_count
    cur_path_windows = [deque() for _ in range(slot_count)]
    cur_path_counts = [dict() for _ in range(slot_count)]
    cur_link_windows = [deque() for _ in range(slot_count)]
    cur_link_counts = [dict() for _ in range(slot_count)]
    rows = []
    suffix = []
    for event in events:
        e, new_t, new_p = event
        if new_t == cur_t and new_p == cur_p:
            rows.append([e, 1, cur_version, cur_version, []])
            continue
        if cur_version >= MAX_COST:
            fail(5)
        (old_worst_sid, old_worst_num, old_worst_den,
         new_worst_sid, new_worst_num, new_worst_den,
         new_reachable, new_no_over, new_latency_ok, migration_ok,
         moves_ok, interval_ok, window_ok, window_demand_ok, distinct_ok,
         distinct_count_ok, path_diversity_ok, link_diversity_ok,
         new_moves, new_clocks, new_windows, new_window_demand,
         new_path_windows, new_path_counts,
         new_link_windows, new_link_counts, scenario_rows) = \
            _config_linkdiv_assess(
                cur_t, new_t, flows, flow_count, prepared, total_demand,
                moved_ppm, move_cap, cur_moves, e, min_gap, cur_clocks,
                window_width, window_cap, cur_windows, cur_window_demand,
                demand_cap, distinct_cap, count_cap,
                cur_path_windows, cur_path_counts, path_cap,
                cur_link_windows, cur_link_counts, link_cap)
        passed = (new_reachable and new_no_over and new_latency_ok
                  and migration_ok and moves_ok and interval_ok
                  and window_ok and window_demand_ok and distinct_ok
                  and distinct_count_ok and path_diversity_ok
                  and link_diversity_ok)
        if passed:
            # Exact comparison of the worst-peak increase against
            # L/1000000: newWorst - oldWorst <= L/1000000.
            delta_num = new_worst_num * old_worst_den \
                - old_worst_num * new_worst_den
            increase_ok = (delta_num * 1000000
                           <= limit_ppm * new_worst_den * old_worst_den)
            if not increase_ok:
                passed = False
        impact = _config_compound_impact(
            old_worst_sid, old_worst_num, old_worst_den,
            new_worst_sid, new_worst_num, new_worst_den, scenario_rows)
        if not passed:
            rows.append([e, 2, cur_version, cur_version, impact])
            return {"op": 36, "mode": mode, "status": 2, "old": v,
                    "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                    "config": pack}
        next_version = cur_version + 1
        rows.append([e, 0, cur_version, next_version, impact])
        suffix.append([next_version, new_t, new_p])
        cur_version = next_version
        cur_t, cur_p = new_t, new_p
        cur_moves = new_moves
        cur_clocks = new_clocks
        cur_windows = new_windows
        cur_window_demand = new_window_demand
        cur_path_windows = new_path_windows
        cur_path_counts = new_path_counts
        cur_link_windows = new_link_windows
        cur_link_counts = new_link_counts
    change_count = len(suffix)

    if base != v:
        # The only tolerated stale base is an exact resend: PACK must
        # already end exactly at the simulated suffix with every entry
        # equal; anything else is a version/suffix conflict.
        if change_count == 0 or v != base + change_count:
            fail(5)
        for offset, entry in enumerate(suffix, start=1):
            if history[base + offset] != entry:
                fail(5)
        return {"op": 36, "mode": mode, "status": 1, "old": base,
                "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}

    if change_count == 0:
        # All events idempotent at the current version: nothing to
        # append, so a commit writes nothing either.
        return {"op": 36, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
                "new": base, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}
    new_pack = {"v": v + change_count, "t": cur_t, "p": cur_p,
                "h": history + suffix}
    if mode == 1:
        _write_state_atomic(pack_path, new_pack)
        applied = True
    else:
        applied = False
    return {"op": 36, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
            "new": v + change_count, "applied": applied, "events": rows,
            "config": new_pack}

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RELAY = os.path.join(HERE, "relay.py")

P = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]


def link(frm, to, cost=1, bw=10000, lat=10, up=True):
    return {"from": frm, "to": to, "cost": cost, "bandwidth": bw,
            "latency": lat, "up": up}


def base_topo(cab=1, cac=1, c7d=1):
    # n0 -> n4 has two equal-length routes that share the n0->a head
    # link: via b (n0,a,b,n4) and via c (n0,a,c,n4). Raising a-b pushes
    # the route via c and raising a-c pushes it back via b. An isolated
    # n5 -> n6 link carries a flow that never migrates. A second
    # independent diamond n7 -> d/e -> n11 carries f2; raising n7-d
    # pushes f2 via e. At equal cost the full-node-sequence tie break
    # picks b before c (and d before e).
    return {"nodes": ["n0", "a", "b", "c", "n4", "n5", "n6",
                      "n7", "d", "e", "n11"],
            "links": [link("n0", "a"),
                      link("a", "b", cab), link("b", "n4"),
                      link("a", "c", cac), link("c", "n4"),
                      link("n5", "n6"),
                      link("n7", "d", c7d), link("d", "n11"),
                      link("n7", "e"), link("e", "n11")]}


# tA ties on cost 3 via b/c and via d/e; tB raises a-b and n7-d so the
# c route and the e route win; tC raises a-c instead (still cheap via
# b), leaving f2 on the d route.
T_A = base_topo()
T_B = base_topo(cab=9, c7d=9)
T_C = base_topo(cac=9)

P1 = ["n0", "a", "b", "n4"]
P2 = ["n0", "a", "c", "n4"]
P3 = ["n7", "d", "n11"]
P4 = ["n7", "e", "n11"]

# Interior transit nodes (endpoints excluded): P1 -> {a,b}, P2 ->
# {a,c}, P3 -> {d}, P4 -> {e}. Retaining P2 then P1 therefore spans
# three distinct transit nodes {a,b,c} even though the two paths share
# a; retaining both routes of f2 spans only {d,e}. The directed-link
# unions stay op 36's: P1/P2 three links each, five together.

# b failed reroutes tA onto the c route; c failed keeps tA on the b
# route and tB there too, so its window stays empty across the event.
SCENARIOS = [["x", ["b"], []], ["z", ["c"], []]]


def flow(fid="f1", src="n0", dst="n4", demand=1, mlat=1000):
    return [fid, src, dst, demand, mlat]


def pack(topo=None, v=0, history=None):
    topo = topo or T_A
    h = history if history is not None else [[0, topo, P]]
    return {"v": v, "t": topo, "p": P, "h": h}


# f1 (demand 1) is the migrating n0->n4 flow, f2 (demand 999 on
# n5->n6) never moves. Generous defaults except the caller overrides
# Z/Y/X.
FLOWS = [flow(), ["f2", "n5", "n6", 999, 1000]]

# Two independently migrating flows on disjoint relay sets.
TWO_FLOWS = [flow(), ["f3", "n7", "n11", 1, 1000]]


def op37(events, flows_=None, z=10, y=10, x=10, w=5, q=10, m=0, b=0,
         h=1000000, u=1000000, n=1000000, l=1000000, c=1000000, r=10,
         d=0, scenarios=None):
    flows_ = FLOWS if flows_ is None else flows_
    return [37, m, b, events, flows_,
            SCENARIOS if scenarios is None else scenarios,
            l, c, r, d, w, q, h, u, n, x, y, z]


class Op37(unittest.TestCase):
    def call(self, op_obj, pk=None, expect_rc=0):
        pk = pk if pk is not None else pack()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            pp = os.path.join(d, "pack.json")
            with open(pp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(pk, f)
            with open(pp, "rb") as fh:
                before = fh.read()
            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, RELAY, "config", pp,
                                json.dumps(op_obj)], capture_output=True,
                               text=True)
            self.assertEqual(r.returncode, expect_rc,
                             "rc=%s err=%s out=%s"
                             % (r.returncode, r.stderr, r.stdout))
            out = json.loads(r.stdout) if r.stdout else None
            with open(pp, "rb") as fh:
                after = fh.read()
            tmps = [name for name in os.listdir(d) if ".tmp." in name]
            return out, before, after, tmps

    def call_raw(self, op_obj, pk=None):
        pk = pk if pk is not None else pack()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            pp = os.path.join(d, "pack.json")
            with open(pp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(pk, f)
            return subprocess.run([sys.executable, RELAY, "config", pp,
                                   json.dumps(op_obj)], capture_output=True)

    def test_preview_pass_renders_transit_fields(self):
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op37([[1, T_B, P]], z=10))
        # Top-level key order stays op 36's exactly.

def test_preview_pass_renders_transit_fields(self):
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op37([[1, T_B, P]], z=10))
        # Top-level key order stays op 36's exactly.
        self.assertEqual(list(out.keys()),
                         ["op", "mode", "status", "old", "new", "applied",
                          "events", "config"])
        self.assertEqual([out["op"], out["mode"], out["status"],
                          out["old"], out["new"], out["applied"]],
                         [37, 0, 0, 0, 1, False])
        self.assertEqual(after, before)
        self.assertEqual(tmps, [])
        row = out["events"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row[0:4], [1, 0, 0, 1])
        scenarios = row[4][3]
        self.assertEqual(len(scenarios), 3)
        # Scenario row: op 36's 18-element shape with
        # maxWindowDistinctTransitNodes inserted after
        # maxWindowDistinctLinks and before pass (19 elements).
        s0 = scenarios[0]
        self.assertEqual(len(s0), 19)
        self.assertEqual(s0[13], 1)             # maxWindowDistinctPaths
        self.assertEqual(s0[14], 3)             # maxWindowDistinctLinks
        self.assertEqual(s0[15], 2)             # maxWindowDistinctTransitNodes
        self.assertIs(s0[16], True)             # pass
        # Flow row gains windowDistinctTransitNodeCount/
        # transitNodeDiversityPass after windowDistinctLinkCount and
        # before linkDiversityPass: 22 elements. P2's interior nodes
        # are a and c: two distinct transit nodes.
        f0 = s0[17][0]
        self.assertEqual(len(f0), 22)
        self.assertEqual(f0,
                         ["f1", 3, 3, 30, 30, P1, P2, True, True, 1,
                          None, None, True, -4, 1, True, 1, 3, 2, True,
                          True, True])
        # The stationary f2 keeps empty path, link, and transit windows.
        self.assertEqual(s0[17][1][14:22],
                         [0, True, 0, 0, 0, True, True, True])
        # In x (b failed) f1 already used the c route at tA; in z
        # (c failed) f1 keeps the b route at tB: neither migrates, so
        # all three windows stay empty and the scenarios pass.
        for sx in scenarios[1:]:
            self.assertEqual(sx[14], 0)
            self.assertEqual(sx[15], 0)
            self.assertIs(sx[16], True)
            self.assertEqual(sx[17][0][7], False)
            self.assertEqual(sx[17][0][16:22], [0, 0, 0, True, True, True])

    def test_z_zero_rejects_first_retained_nodes_keeps_candidate(self):
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op37([[1, T_B, P]], z=0))
        self.assertEqual(out["status"], 2)

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RELAY = os.path.join(HERE, "relay.py")

P = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]


def link(frm, to, cost=1, bw=10000, lat=10, up=True):
    return {"from": frm, "to": to, "cost": cost, "bandwidth": bw,
            "latency": lat, "up": up}


def div_topo(sb=1):
    # s -> d has two routes that diverge at the source itself: via b
    # (s,b,d) and via c (s,c,d). Raising s-b pushes the route onto c,
    # changing the source node's very first hop b -> c. An isolated
    # n5 -> n6 link carries a stationary flow that only pads total
    # demand for the retained-demand window gates.
    return {"nodes": ["s", "b", "c", "d", "n5", "n6"],
            "links": [link("s", "b", sb), link("b", "d"),
                      link("s", "c"), link("c", "d"),
                      link("n5", "n6")]}


# tA ties on cost 2 via b/c and the full-node-sequence tie break picks
# b first; tB raises s-b so the c route (first hop c) wins; back to tA
# restores first hop b.
T_A = div_topo()
T_B = div_topo(sb=9)

# Old/new first hops: tA -> b, tB -> c. Failure of b already forced c
# at tA and failure of c keeps b at tB, so neither failure scenario
# ever migrates.
SCENARIOS = [["x", ["b"], []], ["z", ["c"], []]]

# One migrating source-divergent flow plus a stationary demand-999
# flow that only enlarges the demand denominator.
FLOWS = [["f1", "s", "d", 1, 1000],
         ["f2", "n5", "n6", 999, 1000]]


def head_topo(ab=1, ac=1):
    # A second diamond whose two routes SHARE the source head node a:
    # n0 -> a -> {b,c} -> n4. Rerouting between the branches changes the
    # complete path, links, and interior transit nodes but never the
    # first hop (always a), so the next-hop gate diverges from all of
    # op 35/36/37's gates.
    return {"nodes": ["n0", "a", "b", "c", "n4", "n5", "n6"],
            "links": [link("n0", "a"),
                      link("a", "b", ab), link("b", "n4"),
                      link("a", "c", ac), link("c", "n4"),
                      link("n5", "n6")]}


H_A = head_topo()
H_B = head_topo(ab=9)

HP1 = ["n0", "a", "b", "n4"]
HP2 = ["n0", "a", "c", "n4"]
H_FLOWS = [["f1", "n0", "n4", 1, 1000],
           ["f2", "n5", "n6", 999, 1000]]


def dtop(crd=1):
    # Two-hop [s,r,d] competing with a costly direct [s,d] link.
    return {"nodes": ["s", "r", "d", "z0", "z1"],
            "links": [link("s", "d", 9),
                      link("s", "r", 1), link("r", "d", crd),
                      link("z0", "z1")]}


D0 = dtop(1)
D1 = dtop(9)
D_FLOWS = [["g1", "s", "d", 1, 1000],
           ["g2", "z0", "z1", 999, 1000]]
D_SCN = [["g", ["r"], []]]


def pack(topo=None, v=0, history=None):
    topo = topo or T_A
    h = history if history is not None else [[0, topo, P]]
    return {"v": v, "t": topo, "p": P, "h": h}


def op38(events, flows_=None, scenarios=None, j=10, z=10, y=10, x=10,
         w=5, q=10, m=0, b=0, h=1000000, u=1000000, n=1000000,
         l=1000000, c=1000000, r=10, d=0):
    flows_ = FLOWS if flows_ is None else flows_
    return [38, m, b, events,
            flows_, SCENARIOS if scenarios is None else scenarios,
            l, c, r, d, w, q, h, u, n, x, y, z, j]


class Op38(unittest.TestCase):
    def call(self, op_obj, pk=None, expect_rc=0):
        pk = pk if pk is not None else pack()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            pp = os.path.join(d, "pack.json")
            with open(pp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(pk, f)
            with open(pp, "rb") as fh:
                before = fh.read()
            run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, RELAY, "config", pp,
                                  json.dumps(op_obj)], capture_output=True,
                                 text=True)
            self.assertEqual(run.returncode, expect_rc,
                             "rc=%s err=%s out=%s"
                             % (run.returncode, run.stderr, run.stdout))
            out = json.loads(run.stdout) if run.stdout else None
            with open(pp, "rb") as fh:
                after = fh.read()
            tmps = [name for name in os.listdir(d) if ".tmp." in name]
            return out, before, after, tmps

    def call_raw(self, op_obj, pk=None, raw_text=None):
        pk = pk if pk is not None else pack()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            pp = os.path.join(d, "pack.json")
            with open(pp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(pk, f)
            text = raw_text if raw_text is not None else json.dumps(op_obj)
            return subprocess.run([sys.executable, RELAY, "config", pp,
                                   text], capture_output=True)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # Rendering / field positions
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    def test_preview_pass_renders_nexthop_fields(self):
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op38([[1, T_B, P]], j=10))
        # Top-level key order unchanged.
        self.assertEqual(list(out.keys()),
                         ["op", "mode", "status", "old", "new", "applied",
                          "events", "config"])
        self.assertEqual([out["op"], out["mode"], out["status"],
                          out["old"], out["new"], out["applied"]],
                         [38, 0, 0, 0, 1, False])
        self.assertEqual(after, before)
        self.assertEqual(tmps, [])
        row = out["events"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row[0:4], [1, 0, 0, 1])
        scenarios = row[4][3]
        self.assertEqual(len(scenarios), 3)
        # Scenario row: op 37's 19-element shape with
        # maxWindowDistinctNexthops inserted after
        # maxWindowDistinctTransitNodes and before pass (20 elements).
        s0 = scenarios[0]
        self.assertEqual(len(s0), 20)
        self.assertEqual(s0[13], 1)             # maxWindowDistinctPaths
        self.assertEqual(s0[14], 3)             # maxWindowDistinctLinks
        self.assertEqual(s0[15], 1)             # maxWindowDistinctTransitNodes (c)
        self.assertEqual(s0[16], 1)             # maxWindowDistinctNexthops (c)
        self.assertIs(s0[17], True)             # pass
        # Flow row gains windowDistinctNexthopCount / nexthopDiversityPass
        # after windowDistinctTransitNodeCount and before
        # transitNodeDiversityPass: 24 elements.
        f0 = s0[18][0]
        self.assertEqual(len(f0), 24)
        self.assertEqual(f0,
                         ["f1", 2, 2, 20, 20,
                          ["s", "b", "d"], ["s", "c", "d"], True, True,
                          1, None, None, True, -4, 1, True,
                          1, 3, 1, 1, True, True, True, True])
        # The stationary f2 keeps every window empty.
        self.assertEqual(s0[18][1][14:24],
                         [0, True, 0, 0, 0, 0, True, True, True, True])
        # Failure scenarios do not migrate: their windows stay empty.
        for sx in scenarios[1:]:
            self.assertEqual(sx[15], 0)
            self.assertEqual(sx[16], 0)
            self.assertIs(sx[17], True)
            self.assertEqual(sx[18][0][7], False)
            self.assertEqual(sx[18][0][16:24],
                             [0, 0, 0, 0, True, True, True, True])

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # J = 0 accepts only the empty window
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    def test_j_zero_rejects_first_retained_hop_keeps_candidate(self):
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op38([[1, T_B, P]], j=0))
        self.assertEqual(out["status"], 2)
        self.assertEqual([out["old"], out["new"], out["applied"]],
                         [0, 0, False])
        self.assertEqual(after, before)
        self.assertEqual(tmps, [])
        self.assertEqual([(r[0], r[1]) for r in out["events"]],
                         [(1, 2)])
        s0 = out["events"][0][4][3][0]
        self.assertEqual(s0[16], 1)
        self.assertFalse(s0[17])
        fr = s0[18][0]
        # Candidate post-event values retained: one distinct next hop,
        # J gate failed, transit/link/path gates still fine.
        self.assertEqual(fr[18:24], [1, 1, False, True, True, True])
        # Failure scenarios never moved and still pass.
        for sx in out["events"][0][4][3][1:]:
            self.assertTrue(sx[17])
            self.assertEqual(sx[16], 0)

    def test_j_one_admits_single_first_hop(self):
        out, _, _, _ = self.call(op38([[1, T_B, P]], j=1))
        self.assertEqual(out["status"], 0)
        s0 = out["events"][0][4][3][0]
        self.assertEqual(s0[16], 1)
        self.assertTrue(s0[17])
        self.assertEqual(s0[18][0][19:24], [1, True, True, True, True])

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    # The gate genuinely diverges from path / link / transit gates
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------
    def test_shared_head_hop_counts_once_across_paths(self):
        # H_A -> H_B -> H_A retains HP2 then HP1: two distinct paths,

        # {a,b,c}, but both paths leave the source via the SAME first

            op38(events, flows_=H_FLOWS, w=100, x=2, y=5, z=2, j=1,

    return {"nodes": ["s", "b", "c", "d", "n5", "n6"],
